title: Migration spec: deprecate legacy /v1/generate endpoints and map legacy model IDs to Catalog IDs
creator: Asha Patel
description: Background: Several older clients and SDKs still call the legacy /v1/generate and /v1/embeddings (legacy-model names like redwood-gen-legacy, rwd-embed-v1) endpoints. These endpoints are implemented on older serving paths that limit performance optimizations (no KV prefix caching, older batching heuristics) and prevent consolidating telemetry. Goal: Provide a clear migration path that maps legacy endpoint semantics and model IDs to the supported Redwood Catalog model IDs and new endpoints (/v1/generate-compute /v1/embeddings-batched or unified /v1/completions) with minimal customer friction. This ticket captures product requirements, acceptance criteria, client guidance, timeline, and rollback measures for the deprecation.
scope_included: Identify all legacy endpoints and model name aliases used by top 500 customers (by traffic)
Define deterministic model ID mapping table from legacy names to Catalog IDs and recommended substitute variants
Produce SDK-level compatibility shim proposal and documented examples for Node/Python/Go
Add deprecation response headers and warning payloads for legacy endpoints
Draft and publish customer-facing migration guide and email cadence
Define monitoring, SLOs, and alerting for migration regressions
scope_excluded: Automated in-place remapping at the load-balancer (we will not silently rewrite requests without opt-in)
Major client-side SDK refactors beyond small shims (those remain separate RFCs)
Re-architecting backend model artifacts—model conversion/quantization work is out of scope
acceptance_criteria: Catalog mapping table published and reviewed by Applied ML and Runtime teams
Compatibility shims implemented in open-source SDKs (Node v2.5+, Python v1.9+) with integration tests
Legacy endpoints respond with 299 deprecation warning header and a body that includes migration URL and ETA
Migration guide published in Docs with at least three code examples and a FAQ
Telemetry dashboards show per-customer migration progress; alerts for >5% error increase within 48 hours
Legal & Support communication plan approved and scheduled for top 50 customers
migration_plan: Phase 0 (now - 2026-02-28): inventory - run logs to enumerate legacy endpoints and model alias usage, prioritize top 500 customers
Phase 1 (2026-03-01 - 2026-03-20): build - implement deprecation headers, create mapping table, implement SDK shims, draft docs
Phase 2 (2026-03-21 - 2026-03-31): pilot - enable shim for 10 pilot customers, collect compatibility issues, fix edgecases
Phase 3 (2026-04-01 - 2026-04-10): general warning - send staged emails, enable 299 warnings surface for all legacy calls, publish migration guide
Phase 4 (2026-04-15): soft enforcement - begin returning 410 for undocumented legacy endpoints after grace period for any requests marked opt-out
Phase 5 (2026-04-22): full deprecation - remove legacy endpoint handlers from mainline runtime and route all calls to Catalog-backed endpoints (with final notice)
Post-deprecation (30 days): data cleanup, tombstone telemetry, postmortem and lessons learned
timeline: 2026-02-20: ticket created and initial discovery kickoff
2026-03-01: SDK shim alpha published to npm/pypi as pre-release
2026-04-01: public docs and customer emails sent
2026-04-15: scheduled soft enforcement (410 for clearly deprecated routes)
rollout_strategy: Staged with pilot customers first, then a broad advisory window with automatic deprecation warnings. Maintain backwards-compatible shims in SDKs for two release cycles after hard removal. Allow enterprise customers to opt into extended grace periods via Support ticket. Use canary rollout on Dedicated and Private deployments to validate no regression in P50/P95 latencies.
client_guidance: Action for customers: switch requests to /v1/completions or the new Catalog model ID (see mapping table). Example code for Node, Python, and Go is included in the migration guide.
If your integration uses an SDK older than the shim release, upgrade to the SDK pre-release to receive automatic header warnings and user-friendly exceptions.
If you rely on a model alias that does not have a direct replacement, contact support@redwood.ai to request a migration variant or an enterprise grace period.
Best practice: switch to the Catalog ID and enable caching of model metadata locally to avoid runtime model lookups during requests.
For Dedicated/Private deployments: follow the on-prem migration checklist in the guide—coordinate with Account Engineering for a rolling restart if required.
api_spec_changes: Add 299 Deprecation-Warning response header with JSON body: { "migration_url": "https://docs.redwood.ai/migrations/legacy-generate", "deprecated_on": "2026-04-22" }
Documented model mapping table in API docs under 'Model Migrations' with recommended substitute settings (quantization, temperature equivalence)
Deprecation notes added to /openapi.json with tags and example responses
New structured error codes: MIGRATE_LEGACY_MODEL and LEGACY_ENDPOINT_DEPRECATED
monitoring_and_alerting: Create dashboard: legacy-endpoint-usage (by customer, by model alias)
Alert if migration error rate increases by >5% for any pilot customer for 48h
Alert on spike in 4xx/5xx after soft enforcement, severity P0 if >1% of total traffic is affected
Weekly migration progress report sent to GTM and Support teams
rollback_plan: If pilot reveals critical breakage, revert soft enforcement flags for pilot customers within 2 hours and roll back runtime change
Re-enable legacy handlers in the serving runtime from a hotfix branch within the same day if hard removal causes systemic failures
Communicate rollbacks to customers with a status page entry and targeted emails
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: high-volume clients with embedded SDKs may not update quickly. Mitigation: provide pre-built shims and engage high-touch account teams for manual upgrades.
Risk: slight behavioral drift between legacy models and new Catalog variants. Mitigation: run A/B quality checks using the Optimize evaluation harness and provide recommended parameter adjustments.
Risk: Dedicated/private instances may not pick up runtime changes on schedule. Mitigation: schedule coordinated maintenance windows and provide a rollout checklist for Account Engineering.
